source.title: Open questions regarding the arrow of time

accepted.question_text: In statistical thermodynamics, can the Second Law and the arrow of time be explained without presupposing a direction of time through the very notion of evolution or through time-asymmetric preparation and observation procedures? More specifically, if entropy is defined through probabilities over coarse-grained macrostates built from definite microscopic classical states, what principled justification can be given for the required coarse-graining and ensemble measure without smuggling in a pre-existing temporal asymmetry via state preparation, incomplete observability, or external observers?
accepted.context_brief: Second Law, coarse-graining, and temporal presupposition

evidence.quote: This explanation is incomplete for various reasons. First, the concept of evolution already presumes a direction in time.

The justification of such ensembles by a macroscopic (that is, incompletely defined) preparation procedure would refer to the time-directed concept of preparations as a deus ex machina (similar to Newton’s divine interventions).

accepted.question_text: What is the cosmological origin of the universal thermodynamic arrow of time? In particular, should the present arrow be explained by a special low-entropy condition at the big bang, by a Boltzmann-style giant fluctuation in an eternal universe, or by some other mechanism; and if the low-entropy condition is tied to the big bang, how can one understand the consequences for oscillating-universe models, where the thermodynamic arrow would otherwise have to reverse direction?
accepted.context_brief: Cosmological origin of the thermodynamic arrow

evidence.quote: Its origin has, therefore, usually been discussed in a cosmological context. For example, one may assume a special cosmic initial condition at the big bang.

Boltzmann’s proposal seems to imply, though, that it would then be far more probable if the present state of the universe – including all memories – had just formed in a chance fluctuation, since this state would still possess very low, but much higher entropy than the extremely improbable state in the distant past.

If, on the other hand, the low entropy is related to the special conditions at the big bang, the thermodynamical time arrow would have to change direction in an oscillating universe, while opposite arrows in causally connected parts of the universe seem to be excluded for dynamical reasons.

accepted.question_text: Does stochastic or quantum indeterminism itself define a genuine direction of time, and if so in what form? More concretely, when observed quantum facts arise irreversibly in measurement-like events, should this be understood as a fundamental collapse law, as events outside dynamical law, as a mere increase of information in the Copenhagen sense, as the result of hidden variables, or as branching into Everett worlds; and can any of these interpretations explain the temporal asymmetry without using the same asymmetry they are meant to explain?
accepted.context_brief: Time direction from stochasticity and quantum events

evidence.quote: However, a stochastic law by itself does not necessarily characterize a direction in time.

There is absolutely no consensus among physicists about the interpretation and even the precise dynamical role of this “irreversible coming into being” of the observed facts, such as the click of a counter.

Has it to be regarded as a specific part of the dynamical laws (as assumed in the form of von Neumann’s “first intervention” or more explicitly in collapse theories), as representing events that (according to Pauli) occur outside the laws of nature, as a “normal” increase of information (as claimed in the Copenhagen interpretation), as determined by hidden variables that are not counted in conventional ensemble entropy (as in Bohm’s theory), or as the consequence of inderministically splitting observers (as in Everett’s interpretation)?

accepted.question_text: Why do electromagnetic absorbers, and more generally physical absorptive processes, pick out only one temporal direction? In the case of retarded versus advanced Maxwell fields, if absorbers and thermalization can account for retarded shadows and the absence of incoming high-frequency radiation, what explains the fact that all absorbers absorb in the same time direction rather than admitting the time-reversed alternative with advanced correlations?

evidence.quote: This asymmetry may be understood as a consequence of the presence of absorbers (including the early radiation era of our universe).
But why do all absorbers absorb in one and the same direction of time only?
This absence of advanced correlations is even “probable”, while the low-entropy initial condition that leads to retarded correlations – such as a special initial µ-space distribution ρµ – is not.

accepted.question_text: What is the precise physical content of the low-entropy initial condition that gives rise to the arrow of time? Since different Zwanzig projections and relevance concepts can be useful for defining macroscopic entropy in different situations, which aspect of the universe’s initial state is the real, objective low-entropy property that underwrites temporal asymmetry rather than merely reflecting a convenient coarse-graining choice?
accepted.context_brief: Precise nature of the low-entropy initial condition

evidence.quote: While the precise definition of entropy (its specific relevance concept or Zwanzig projection) is in principle a matter of convenience, the initial cosmic low-entropy condition that would “cause” an arrow of time must represent a real property of the universe, and its precise nature should therefore be revealed.

accepted.question_text: Is the relevant low-entropy condition of the early universe best understood as primordial homogeneity, as Penrose’s vanishing-Weyl-tensor condition on past singularities, or as some closely related condition; and if the Weyl condition cannot be explained by absorptive matter in the way electromagnetic retardation can, must it instead be taken as the law-like ingredient that establishes the causal asymmetry of the universe by excluding future-relevant initial correlations?
accepted.context_brief: Initial homogeneity and the Weyl tensor condition

evidence.quote: Therefore, the initial homogeneity of the universe becomes a major candidate for the specific low entropy condition that characterizes this universe.
Roger Penrose has formulated this condition in general relativity by postulating a vanishing Weyl tensor on all past singularities.
It may then itself have to establish the causal nature of the universe, that is, it would have to be responsible for the absence of future-relevant initial correlations.

accepted.question_text: How should quantum theory account for the arrow of time in cosmology: through a genuine collapse law or through Everettian branching plus decoherence, and what initial condition is needed in either case? In particular, if a non-unitary collapse law has never been experimentally confirmed and Everett branching remains a live alternative, how is the time arrow of decoherence to be grounded in the initial global wave function so that recoherence is suppressed and quasi-classical worlds arise with a definite temporal orientation?

evidence.quote: a non-unitary modification of the Schrödinger equation that would satisfactorily describe it has never been experimentally confirmed. Therefore, Everett’s “branching” of the quantum universe (including all observers) into different autonomous components describing quasi-classical “worlds” must be taken seriously as an alternative.

While the collapse would define a time-asymmetric law, the time arrow of decoherence (retarded entanglement) must again be explained by means of an initial condition – now for the global wave function.

accepted.question_text: In the quantum-gravitational treatment of black holes, should one impose a time-symmetric Weyl-tensor condition on all spacelike singularities, and would doing so eliminate genuine black-hole interiors, horizons, or information loss? Because the black-hole interior is causally inaccessible and quantum gravity no longer sharply distinguishes past from future singularities, the unresolved issue is whether a symmetric singularity condition is the correct way to understand black-hole entropy and avoid the information-loss paradox.
accepted.context_brief: Black holes, singularities, and information loss

evidence.quote: This leaves much freedom for the unknowable physics inside. In particular, quantum gravity does not allow distinguishing between past and future singularities any more (see below).

Therefore, one can only postulate a Weyl tensor condition on all space-like singularities. Such a time-symmetric condition is not only compatible with all observations – it may even prevent black hole interiors and horizons to form (thus avoiding any genuine information loss paradox).

accepted.question_text: How do physical time and its arrow emerge in quantum gravity when the fundamental Wheeler-DeWitt equation has no external time parameter? More specifically, if the quantum-gravitational wave functional satisfies HΨ = 0 and there is no external variable t with respect to which a time direction can be defined, under what assumptions and through what mechanism can one recover an effective physical time and a corresponding arrow of time from intrinsic variables and semiclassical structure?
accepted.context_brief: Emergence of time in Wheeler-DeWitt quantum gravity

evidence.quote: Since the Schrödinger equation now takes the form ∂tΨ = 0, there
exists no time parameter any more that could be used to formulate a direction in time.
However, the physical concept of time – and even its arrow – can be recovered in a satisfactory way under very reasonable assumptions.

accepted.question_text: Can the global intrinsic dynamics of the Wheeler-DeWitt framework determine the initial conditions of the partial Schrödinger waves that appear in the semiclassical WKB regime? Since the WKB approximation yields approximately autonomous matter-wave evolution along quasi-classical geometries but does not by itself justify an ensemble of trajectories, the unresolved problem is how the full, timeless quantum state fixes the initial data for the branch-dependent partial waves observed as evolving quasi-classical worlds.
accepted.context_brief: Initial conditions for partial Schrödinger waves

evidence.quote: Note that this WKB approximation does not by itself justify an ensemble of trajectories, since it preserves the global superposition of all partial waves that evolve along different WKB trajectories
The global intrinsic dynamics would be required, though, to derive initial conditions for all partial Schrödinger waves, to be used in the WKB region of geometry (at some distance from the big bang).

accepted.question_text: In loop quantum cosmology, what physical meaning, if any, should be assigned to negative values of the scale factor a after continuing the Wheeler-DeWitt dynamics through a = 0, and how can that continuation be reconciled with the thermodynamic arrow? If negative a is interpreted as a pre-big-bang phase, one must explain how WKB time could continue through a = 0 and how a low-entropy state at a = 0 could have been preceded by an even lower-entropy state at a < 0 without forcing a reversal of the thermodynamic arrow in an oscillating-universe picture.
accepted.context_brief: Negative scale factor and pre-big-bang interpretation

evidence.quote: Since the WKB times, which represent classical time, can not be continued through a = 0, the interpretation of negative values of a as representing pre-big-bang times is highly questionable.

It would be hard to understand how the low entropy state at a = 0 could have been “preceded” by an even lower entropy at a < 0 in order to avoid a reversal of the thermodynamical arrow in the classical picture of an oscillating universe.
